head: mhw decides their flags
why: `mhw` with no argument prints the whole usage text, which was workstation.py's docstring. Its closing paragraph said that 'this file' decides the installers' flags; the file is gone, so the Node text says 'mhw'. The usage paragraph `mhw --help` prints is word for word the same (steps 0 to 2 are compared unchanged).

head: node: modules only, Node 26 or later \(engines\.node\)\.
why: The same text's last paragraph named the runtime: 'Standard library only, Python 3.9+.' was true of workstation.py and is false of the Node command, which imports node: modules only and needs the node engines.node names.

head:
{4}"/bin/sh",
(?= {4}"<INSTALL_MANAGED>"(,
 {4}"--root=[^"]*")?
 {3}\])
replace: "<the sh that renders the admin stage>",
why: A hardening (test/lifecycle/admin-line.test.js only): workstation.py ran the owner-side render of install-managed.sh, and every install.sh step, as ["sh", script], so the first sh on PATH ran them; the Node commands run /bin/sh by absolute path, as mhw check already does (src/commands/check.js), so no PATH entry decides which shell runs the installers. The root command line itself (the sudo call and its arguments) is unchanged and compared.
